radicals.name: TREE
radicals.origin: A trunk with branches above and roots below. On the left its last stroke shortens to a dot.
radicals.clue: trees and things made of wood
ex: the everyday word for a tree
radicals.watch: Look-alike: 禾 (grain), as in 秋 (autumn), is 木 with one extra stroke across the top. And 机 (jī, machine) carries wood because the first machines were wooden.

radicals.name: GRASS
radicals.origin: Two small shoots pushing out of the ground, joined into one line with two ticks. It always sits on top.
ex: the radical is named after it
radicals.watch: 药 (yào, medicine) has grass because medicine came from herbs. 蓝 (lán, blue) has it because blue dye came from the indigo plant.

radicals.name: BAMBOO
radicals.origin: 竹 is two bamboo stalks with drooping leaves. On top of a character the stalks disappear and only the two leaf tufts stay.
radicals.clue: bamboo and things once made from it
ex: a bamboo handle over a tuft of hair 毛
woven from bamboo, as in 篮球 basketball
radicals.watch: Before paper, books were strips of bamboo tied together. That is why words about writing and order carry bamboo: 第 (number in a series), 答 (to answer), 等 (to rank, to wait). 笑 (xiào, to laugh) is harder to explain.

radicals.name: ANIMAL
radicals.origin: 犬 is an old word for dog. Stood up on its hind legs on the left of a character, it became 犭 and now marks beasts in general.
ex: its sound part 苗 is read miáo, like a meow
radicals.watch: Not every animal lives here. Horses 马, cows 牛, sheep 羊, birds 鸟 and fish 鱼 are radicals of their own. 犭 also marks wild behaviour: 狂 (crazy), 猛 (fierce).

radicals.name: BUG
radicals.origin: The picture began as a snake with a big head. It grew to cover every small creature that is not a beast, a bird or a fish.
ex: small creatures of the water count too
radicals.watch: 虹 (hóng, rainbow) is in this family because people once pictured the rainbow as a great serpent arching across the sky.
